evidence: In the Oct 21 2026 debate he defended his ad's call to suspend the federal fuel tax until the Iran war ends, calling it a short-term stopgap for farmers.
Called the Iran war an illegal offensive war and pledged to bring a bill in January forcing the president to end it quickly (debate, Oct 21 2026).
Original cosponsor, S.J.Res.1, Cruz's constitutional amendment to limit congressional terms (Jan 2025).
Sponsor, National Right to Work Act (reintroduced Feb 2025), which would bar union-dues requirements; the PRO Act does the opposite, so a related but different policy.
Voted for H.R.8369, the Israel Security Assistance Support Act, which barred withholding U.S. weapons from Israel (May 16 2024, 224-187).
In a Jan 2022 floor speech opposed Democrats' push to end the 60-vote rule, saying a 51% win shouldn't mean getting everything; voted to keep it (Jan 19 2022).
Voted to sustain the chair and block Democrats' talking-filibuster carve-out for voting rights, a narrower change than abolition (Jan 19 2022, 52-48).
Voted to block Democrats' talking-filibuster carve-out (Jan 19 2022, 52-48), but was later named among GOP senators urging weakening the 60-vote rule (May 2026).
Cosponsor, S.J.Res.2 (115th), Cruz's term-limits amendment (3 House terms, 2 Senate), saying limits keep politicians honest (Feb 2017); not on the 2025 version.
Sponsor, AI Emergency Button Act, requiring advanced AI models to have an emergency kill switch; sought unanimous passage Sep 2026 (blocked by Paul); a narrower bill than broad AI guardrails.
Sponsor, Dependent Care FSA Expansion Act, raising the limit on pre-tax dependent care accounts (Dec 2024); a narrower, related approach, not a 7% cap.
Signed a letter with Lankford objecting to Biden's plan to grant legal status to undocumented spouses, calling it amnesty (Jun 2024); a related executive action.
As a House member voted against H.R.800, the Employee Free Choice Act, an earlier union-organizing bill (Mar 1 2007, 241-185); not the PRO Act itself.
As a House member voted against H.R.1905, giving DC a voting House seat, a narrower step than statehood (Apr 19 2007, 241-177).
As a House member voted against H.R.626, four weeks of paid parental leave for federal workers, a narrower policy (Jun 4 2009, 258-154).
In an Aug 2015 GOP debate said he had been fighting single-payer for a decade; strongly opposes government-run health care.
Has argued punishing the rich costs the poor jobs (Aug 2012) and backs a flat tax and repealing capital gains and estate tax hikes; no OBBBA-specific statement.
